sents.t: For the last two months, I have been running three times a week.
It all started at the gym in June, when Jasmine put up a poster: the Oakville Half Marathon, October 10th.
Thirteen point one miles.
“You should sign up,” she said.
“You’ve been coming to the gym for six months, and you’re much stronger now.”
I laughed.
A year ago, I couldn’t run to the bus stop.
But I signed up.
Jasmine made me a training plan.
Every Sunday, my long run gets one mile longer.
On the other days, I do short, fast runs.
It hasn’t been easy.
In July, it was ninety-five degrees, so I had to run at six in the morning.
Last week, I got a blister on my foot, and my knees have been hurting since Saturday.
“Have you been drinking enough water?” Jasmine asked.
“And how old are your shoes?”
My running shoes were three years old.
She sent me to a running store, where a man filmed me on a treadmill and found the right shoes for my feet.
Now I’ve been running nine miles on Sundays without stopping.
Rosa and Max wait for me at the end of the trail with a bottle of water.
Four more weeks to go!

comp.q: How often has Sam been running?
comp.fa: سام هر چند وقت یک بار دویده است؟

comp.q: How long is a half marathon?
Why did Sam run at six in the morning in July?
o: It was too hot later in the day.
comp.fa: چرا سام در ژوئیه ساعت شش صبح می‌دوید؟

comp.q: What was the problem with Sam’s shoes?
What does “four more weeks to go” mean?
o: He runs four weeks a year.
comp.fa: «four more weeks to go» یعنی چه؟

comp.q: How has Sam probably changed since last year?
o: He has moved to a new city.
comp.fa: سام احتمالاً از پارسال تا حالا چطور تغییر کرده است؟
